title: ICATT co-writes Common Ground, so it offers influence as well as delivery
content:
ICATT's qualification is not that it uses Common Ground but that it helped write it. The record has it co-developing Common Ground standards alongside VNG, Den Haag, Utrecht, Rotterdam, Maykin and Ritense — that is, alongside both the standards owner and the municipalities that adopt first.

On the delivery side it built KISS, an open-source product, with seven Dimpact municipalities and Gemeente Utrecht. The same firm therefore appears on both sides of the Dutch municipal stack: inside the group setting the architecture, and shipping open-source product into the municipalities that must conform to it. It positions itself as Common Ground, transparent and open.

Commercially this makes ICATT a two-for-one. A lead offering only delivery has to be persuaded that a new stack fits its next project; a lead inside the standards group can affect what the next generation of projects is required to look like. That is slower leverage but more durable, and it is why several Dutch entries in this set are valued partly for their proximity to the standards conversation.
